newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil rail auction to go ahead as scheduled Fri.
newsitem.headline: Brazil rail auction to go ahead as scheduled Fri.

text.p: The filet mignon of Brazil's federal railway network comes will be on the block as scheduled Friday on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange, but with only one bidder in the running the auction promises to be dull.

The choice 1,674-km southeast section of the federal railway network runs through Brazil's industrial heartland of Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais states, providing a link between iron ore mines, three large steel firms and Brazil's main ports.

The future operator of the southeast railway section will also benefit from an accord with Sao Paulo state's railway Fepasa which allows for the southeast section to run trains on Fepasa's tracks, said a federal railway spokesman.

The MRS Logistica consortium, which is being led by steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN), is expected to acquire the 30-year concession to operate the southeast section for the minimum price of 888.9 million reais ($888.9 million).
The consortium also includes steel firm Cosigua, mining companies MBR and Ferteco, fertilizer company Ultrafertil, transport groups Celato and Interferrea and two pension funds.

MRS would have 30 days to pay 30 percent of the sale price with the rest payable in quarterly installments throughout the 30-year period starting one year after the acquisition, said the federal railway spokesman.

Under the terms of the privatization model, the consortium would have to invest at least $227 million in the railway section over the first six years of the concession and $1.41 billion in the remaining time period, he said.
The southeast railway section, which accounts for 40 percent of the federal railway's turnover, is the only section to post a regular annual profit, the spokesman said.
In 1995, the southeast section had a turnover of 353.2 million reais ($353.2 million), compared with the federal railway's total turnover of 881.7 million reais ($881.7 million).

The southeast section's 401 locomotives and 11,086 wagons mainly transport iron ore followed by cement and steel products. Last year, a total freight volume of 20.2 billion tonnes per kilometer was transported on the railway section.

The southeast section is the third of the federal railway's six stretches included in the country's privatization program. Earlier this year, Brazil sold the concessions to operate the center-east and west sections.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
